nodes.label: Conventional lint workflow
nodes.rationale: Rules come from commitlint.config.mjs, so this check and the local .husky/commit-msg hook can never disagree.

nodes.label: Issue title lint workflow
nodes.rationale: GitHub cannot reject an issue at creation time, so an invalid title is labelled invalid-title, answered with a comment explaining the format when opened, and the check fails; the label clears once the title passes.

nodes.label: Lint workflow (formatting)
nodes.rationale: The pre-commit hook rewrites staged files rather than failing, and --no-verify, web edits and fork contributors skip it entirely, so this CI check is the one that actually holds.

nodes.label: .husky/commit-msg hook
nodes.rationale: Blocks a commit whose message is not conventional, using the same commitlint rule set as the workflows.

nodes.label: .husky/pre-commit hook
nodes.rationale: Rewrites staged files rather than failing.

nodes.label: .husky/pre-push hook
nodes.rationale: Blocks a push straight to the default branch, so work reaches main only through a pull request. Like every local hook it is fast feedback that --no-verify can skip.

nodes.label: RTK condensed command output
nodes.rationale: Output is condensed to save tokens while keeping every signal, so treat it as the complete result, run commands normally and batch related commands to avoid extra turns.

nodes.label: bun (package manager and script runner)
nodes.rationale: bun, not npm or yarn: bun install and bun run lint are the project entry points.

nodes.label: Conventional Commits
nodes.rationale: Used for commit subjects, issue titles and pull request titles alike, so one glance at any of the three tells you what kind of change it is. Format: <type>[optional scope]: <description>, where the scope is an optional noun naming the part of the codebase touched and the description is imperative, lower case, with no trailing period.

nodes.label: Feature request issue form
nodes.rationale: Also the starting point for issues that are neither bug nor feature; the author changes the title type and the enhancement label to match.

nodes.label: Pull request template
nodes.rationale: Enforces nothing; it reminds the author of the title format, atomic commits, breaking-change marking and bun run lint.

nodes.label: Query the graph before reading source
nodes.norm_label: query the graph before reading source
nodes.rationale: graphify query, path and explain return a scoped subgraph, usually much smaller than GRAPH_REPORT.md or raw grep output; the wiki index serves broad navigation and GRAPH_REPORT.md only broad architecture review.

nodes.label: Run graphify update after modifying code
nodes.norm_label: run graphify update after modifying code
nodes.rationale: Keeps the graph current; the update is AST-only, so it has no API cost.

nodes.label: rtk proxy fallback
nodes.rationale: Re-run a command through rtk proxy only when its result is unusable: empty when output was expected, contradicting its exit code, or garbled.

nodes.label: Prettier owns syntax, not prose
nodes.rationale: bun run lint checks the whole tree and lint-staged fixes staged files on commit, so do not hand-format around it. printWidth applies to code and proseWrap is left at preserve, so Prettier never rewraps a Markdown paragraph: the 80-character limit is the author's to keep and nothing checks it.

nodes.label: Atomic commits
nodes.rationale: One reason to change per commit, and every commit builds on its own; a subject that needs the word 'and' is two commits.

nodes.label: Branch naming (<type>/<short-description>)
nodes.rationale: Reuses the commit types but is not machine-checked; it is a courtesy to whoever reads the branch list.

nodes.label: Breaking change marker (! and BREAKING CHANGE footer)
nodes.norm_label: breaking change marker (! and breaking change footer)
nodes.rationale: A breaking change takes a ! before the colon and explains itself in the body or in a BREAKING CHANGE: footer.

nodes.label: gh pr create --fill-first
nodes.rationale: --fill takes the title from the branch name on a branch with more than one commit, which the title check rejects. --fill-first takes it from the first commit, which may not describe the whole branch, so pass --title when it does not.

nodes.label: Conventional issue and pull request titles
nodes.norm_label: conventional issue and pull request titles

nodes.norm_label: local hook setup (bun install, then uv tool install graphifyy)

nodes.label: Brushed metal cap
nodes.rationale: The weakest stretch of the subject outline: its top edge (luma about 170) is only about 36 levels from the paper above it (about 206), against 150-170 levels at the glass sides, so a subject selection is most likely to clip or bleed there. Lit from the left, it has a bright vertical specular band (luma about 245) left of centre and a shaded right half (50-95).

nodes.label: Cast shadow
nodes.rationale: Lit from the left, the bottle throws a soft shadow back and to the right across the floor (about x 900-1300, y 700-830), about 60 levels darker than the paper. Its core (about RGB 155,139,139) is cooler than the warm paper (about 210,199,185), likely light filtered through the cobalt glass, so a kept shadow must keep that tint. It is what 'keep the product shadow' protects when the background is removed.

nodes.label: Cobalt glass bottle
nodes.rationale: The subject to select and mask, centred in the frame: the glass spans about x 639-894 and y 310-820, and with the cap the subject runs from y 148 to about 840. Its sides contrast strongly with the paper (glass luma 40-60 against about 215). The translucent glass lightens and desaturates from the shoulder (luma 13-27) to the lower body (38-54) and turns nearly neutral at the heavy base where it meets the floor. It has no label, so an instruction to leave the label unchanged has nothing to protect here.

nodes.label: Dust specks
nodes.rationale: At least a dozen distinct dark spots on the floor of the sweep, the clearest near (1254, 825), (177, 871) and (40, 840), up to about 145 levels darker than the surrounding paper. Each is only a few pixels across, and smaller still once Photopea fits the photograph into the agent's 1440x900 view, which makes them easy for the agent to miss.

nodes.label: Glass reflections
nodes.rationale: A bright window-like highlight on the upper-left shoulder (about x 690-750, y 378-412) and fainter vertical streaks down the left third of the body (around x 690-730, luma 64-107 against 19-45 for the glass), consistent with light from the left. They are what an instruction to clean the reflections targets, but they also model the bottle's roundness, so removing them outright would flatten it.

nodes.label: Paper crease
nodes.rationale: A vertical crease right of the bottle and the strongest line in the background: mean horizontal gradient at x 1118-1136 is 1.9-2.2 against 0.93 elsewhere, and it is visible from top to bottom. A defect to heal on a kept background, or one a cut-out discards.

nodes.label: Paper sweep backdrop
nodes.rationale: What any background edit acts on. The paper is dull rather than white (median image luma 202), warm (red above blue by 20-35 levels), and unevenly lit, falling from about RGB 232,223,210 at the left edge to about 196,181,163 at the right, so removing, evening or neutralising it is visible work.

nodes.label: Sample photo generation prompt (unbranded cobalt-blue glass cosmetic bottle on a warm paper sweep)
nodes.norm_label: sample photo generation prompt (unbranded cobalt-blue glass cosmetic bottle on a warm paper sweep)
nodes.rationale: Deliberately raw rather than polished: dust specks, mild reflection distractions, paper wrinkles and a restrained cast shadow give a retouching demo visible work, while no text, label, logo, trademark, watermark or already-perfect retouching keeps it original.

nodes.label: Photopea postMessage protocol
nodes.rationale: A String is executed as a script, an ArrayBuffer is opened as a file (sidestepping CORS for URL loads), and an export arrives as an ArrayBuffer followed by "done" with no filename, MIME type or correlation id; startup configuration rides in the URL hash; export is saveToOE("psd").

nodes.label: Photopea known traps
nodes.rationale: Trap 1 and the Action Manager stub were confirmed by reading the shipped bundle; traps 2 to 6 (ES3 dialect, poisoned interpreter needing a reload, silent no-ops verified by reading state back, text layers needing two seconds, slow boot) are third-party recon until spike B1 confirms them.

nodes.norm_label: spike b1: verify the image-in, psd-out round trip
nodes.rationale: Day 0, half a day; confirms or strikes out each unverified Photopea trap.

nodes.label: Document-count snapshot before file delivery
nodes.rationale: Photopea can finish processing a truncated file without creating a document, so the loader snapshots the document count and requires exactly one newly appended document before selecting or renaming it.

nodes.label: Per-bridge FIFO for complete document opens
nodes.norm_label: per-bridge fifo for complete document opens
nodes.rationale: The bridge per-command queue did not protect the whole count-to-verification workflow, so complete opens share an internal FIFO keyed by bridge identity across loader instances, held through Move-tool selection; failed calls do not block later work, and validation and byte copying happen before queueing.

nodes.label: Unique app.echoToOE sentinel per scripted call
nodes.norm_label: unique app.echotooe sentinel per scripted call
nodes.rationale: "done" is not a reliable terminator because some operations emit their own mid-script, so a naive wait desynchronises; a sentinel timeout means reload the frame, not retry.

nodes.label: Reusable Photopea bridge boot
nodes.rationale: From the September 14 review: concurrent boot calls share one readiness wait, a successful boot is cached and a failed one permits a fresh host, cleanup messages cannot satisfy a retry, and commandTimeoutMs bounds each message wait. The review also added header-field validation before navigation and applied the transport viewport to injected pages.

nodes.label: Pre-warmed editor sessions
nodes.rationale: About two seconds of boot plus a five-second first round trip overruns the five-second NFR-3 budget, so warming the session before the button is load-bearing and the first thing to measure.

Commit 48fade8 (fix(editor): export the recorded document preview) added it because the recorded FakeEditorSession previously reused the 1440x900 Photopea viewport frame as its preview; exportPreview() must return the flattened document PNG that EditorSession documents for FR-28, and a test asserts the preview is 640x480 and differs from the frame. nodes.rationale: Stable machine codes with plain-language reasons; a route never returns a stack, credential, raw provider error or Browserbase connection URL.

nodes.label: RunRegistry background event pump with sixty-minute terminal retention
nodes.norm_label: runregistry background event pump with sixty-minute terminal retention
nodes.rationale: The pump stores ordered history, keeps a snapshot and broadcasts without depending on a connected page, so browser disconnects cannot pause a run. Terminal metadata is retained sixty minutes for launch-day reconnects but is not user history, and releaseSecrets() runs in finally on every terminal path.

nodes.label: Signed visitor cookie and HMAC visitor key (TRUST_PROXY_HOPS)
nodes.norm_label: signed visitor cookie and hmac visitor key (trust_proxy_hops)
nodes.rationale: A signed HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax cookie holds a random identifier; the database key is an HMAC of it and the normalized client address, so neither raw address nor signing secret is stored. Forwarded addresses are trusted only at the exact configured hop depth.

nodes.label: SSE sequence-id replay and sessionStorage reconnect
nodes.norm_label: sse sequence-id replay and sessionstorage reconnect
nodes.rationale: Each event carries its zero-based sequence as the SSE id; a reload restores the runId from sessionStorage, fetches the snapshot, reconnects with EventSource, and the client reducer ignores duplicate ids.

nodes.label: Run registry
nodes.rationale: Server-side run state keyed by runId; the page holds only the id, so a reload re-subscribes instead of restarting (FR-14).

nodes.label: Run admission order (body ceiling, instruction, image, visitor identity, meter, upload, RunHandle)
nodes.norm_label: run admission order (body ceiling, instruction, image, visitor identity, meter, upload, runhandle)
nodes.rationale: Ordered to avoid paid work for invalid or refused requests: an admission or persistence failure never starts a browser session, and a failure after quota reservation releases the reservation.

nodes.label: Single long-lived server process (not serverless)
nodes.rationale: A run is a stateful conversation lasting minutes that holds a browser session and streams frames, so it cannot resume from nothing on a cold invocation.

nodes.label: Browserbase probe usage against a deployed /photopea-host
nodes.norm_label: browserbase probe usage against a deployed /photopea-host
nodes.rationale: Prints the session id, public live-view URL and cold-start time; never prints the API key or private CDP connection URL, and requests session release in a finally block.

nodes.label: Image resolution vs screenshot viewport
nodes.rationale: The photograph opens and exports at full resolution while the screenshot is the 1440x900 browser viewport, so the no-downscaling rule is about screenshots only.

nodes.label: Screenshot policy: 1440x900, detail original, no downscaling
nodes.norm_label: screenshot policy: 1440x900, detail original, no downscaling
nodes.rationale: The integration guide warns against high and low detail for computer use; downscaling would force remapping model coordinates, a bug generator. A frame costs about 1,570 tokens.

nodes.label: Better/Best Rule
nodes.rationale: Documentation review sets a lower bar per change so that more changes happen: reviewers approve quickly, suggest alternatives and start their own follow-ups for substantial changes, and authors capitulate early instead of arguing.

nodes.label: Code spans for inline code and escaping
nodes.community_name: Code spans for inline code and escaping
nodes.norm_label: code spans for inline code and escaping
nodes.rationale: Backticks render short code, field names and generic file names literally, and stop fake paths or example URLs from turning into bad autolinks.

nodes.label: Informative link titles
nodes.rationale: Readers scan rather than read, and link text such as 'here', 'link' or a bare URL tells them nothing; write the sentence naturally, then wrap its most descriptive phrase.

nodes.label: Lazy list numbering and 4-space nested indent
nodes.community_name: Lazy list numbering and 4-space nested indent
nodes.norm_label: lazy list numbering and 4-space nested indent
nodes.rationale: Lazy 1. numbering suits long lists that may change, while short stable lists read better fully numbered in source; a 4-space indent keeps wrapped and nested text aligned.

nodes.label: Preserve original product name capitalization
nodes.rationale: Names of products, tools and binaries keep their original capitalization.

nodes.label: Single H1 heading
nodes.rationale: One H1 serves as the document title; every later heading is H2 or deeper.

nodes.label: [TOC] directive after the introduction
nodes.rationale: Use it unless all content is above the fold. Placement matters for screen readers and keyboard users, because [TOC] inserts the table of contents into the DOM wherever the directive appears.

nodes.label: Unique, complete heading names
nodes.rationale: Link anchors are generated from headings, so unique, fully descriptive names keep those anchors intuitive and clear.

nodes.label: Adobe Photoshop API v2
nodes.rationale: /v2/execute-actions and /v2/create-composite return a layered PSD server-side with no browser or GUI; only an enterprise contract, a commercial rather than technical moat, stands in the way.

nodes.label: Adobe Firefly Creative Production (Remove Background preset, masked layered PSD)
nodes.norm_label: adobe firefly creative production (remove background preset, masked layered psd)
nodes.rationale: Since October 28, 2025 Adobe's paid plans include the bulk Remove Background preset, returning a layered PSD with a masked image layer for 40 generative credits an output, so a mask no longer sets anything apart.

nodes.rationale: A flat JPEG cannot absorb the client's next change request, so the AI saved nothing; the gap is the format of the output, not quality.

nodes.norm_label: human retouching price ceiling ($0.39-$2.00 per image)

nodes.norm_label: missing demand signal for layered-psd delivery

nodes.norm_label: commercial gate (risk 1: the commercial case vs the survey)

nodes.rationale: Parse the exported file and assert layer count, human names and at least one editable mask or adjustment, then open it manually once a day in Photoshop, Affinity and GIMP.

nodes.label: Layered PSD output (the wedge)
nodes.rationale: A diffusion model cannot emit a layer stack at any quality because a layer stack is an edit history, a difference in kind. Pitch: AI retouching that returns a layered PSD, not a flat JPEG.

nodes.norm_label: remaining gap: no self-serve single-pass psd known to be named, masked and adjustment-layered
nodes.rationale: Adobe's self-serve plans already ship the mask and BRIA ships raster layers, so what remains is adjustment layers and human layer names: narrower than the pitch.

nodes.label: Risk: the scripting escape hatch
nodes.rationale: Scripting the retouching decisions rather than loading and exporting would let any model do the job; holding that line is a discipline problem, not a technical one.

nodes.label: Async tool calling (primitive)
nodes.rationale: Dead: an orchestration ergonomics win that a job queue replicates and the user cannot feel.

nodes.label: Million-token single-pass context (primitive)
nodes.rationale: Clears the Swap Test only for inconsistency tasks: retrieval needs a query, and a contradiction has none.

nodes.label: Persisted reasoning and notes (primitive)
nodes.rationale: Dead: Astra has no cross-conversation memory, so persistence built on top of it works on any model.

nodes.label: Programmatic tool calling and orchestration (primitive)
nodes.rationale: Dead: a cost and latency optimisation; batch work that does pass does so for whole-corpus reasoning, not loop-writing.

nodes.label: WebMCP
nodes.rationale: Dead by design: an open standard that decouples the page from the model scores zero on model leverage; worth it only as a surface attached to an Astra-only capability.

nodes.label: Inferred judging rubric (WebMCP Challenge criteria)
nodes.rationale: OpenAI published no judging criteria, so ideas are scored on the four equally weighted WebMCP Challenge criteria plus launch legibility and showcase-ability, an inference from the nearest comparable contest.

nodes.label: Swap Test
nodes.rationale: Swap Astra for another model and ask whether the product gets slightly worse or stops existing; applied to user-visible behaviour, never to the implementation, because judges score the product.

nodes.label: Scripted vs GUI-driven split (the line that protects the premise)
nodes.norm_label: scripted vs gui-driven split (the line that protects the premise)
nodes.rationale: Loading, layer naming, export and viewport are scripted; selecting the subject, masks, adjustments and judging the edit are driven through the GUI. Scripting the retouching decisions would let any model do the job.

nodes.label: Security and error-handling rules (textContent not innerHTML, restrictive CSP, egress policy, export before release)
nodes.norm_label: security and error-handling rules (textcontent not innerhtml, restrictive csp, egress policy, export before release)
nodes.rationale: Configuration errors name variables, never values; every completion, cancellation, timeout and error path exports first when possible and releases the browser session in finally; recoverable errors stay visible without ending the SSE stream, and unrecoverable ones end once with a specific public reason.

nodes.label: Filename verification through Document.source
nodes.rationale: Photopea Document.name read-back drops text from the first period onward, so the loader sets a display stem and verifies the complete filename through the documented Document.source identifier.

nodes.label: Simplicity First
nodes.rationale: Minimum code that solves the problem and nothing speculative: no unrequested features, single-use abstractions, unrequested configurability or error handling for impossible scenarios.

nodes.label: Surgical Changes
nodes.rationale: Touch only what you must and clean up only your own mess; every changed line should trace directly to the user's request.

nodes.label: Think Before Coding
nodes.rationale: Don't assume, don't hide confusion, surface tradeoffs: state assumptions, present competing interpretations, push back when a simpler approach exists, and stop to ask when something is unclear.

nodes.label: ComputerAction type
nodes.rationale: Mirrors the computer tool action schema exactly, so a computer_call passes through without translation and the tool fallback stays a swap rather than a rewrite.

nodes.label: Bring-your-own-key
nodes.rationale: The release valve for launch-day traffic: it decouples our cost from our popularity on the one day popularity spikes.

nodes.label: Quadratic screenshot-history cost (~$3.50 cached vs ~$14.50 uncached per image)
nodes.norm_label: quadratic screenshot-history cost (~$3.50 cached vs ~$14.50 uncached per image)
nodes.rationale: Forty 1,570-token screenshots resend about 1.3M input tokens cumulatively; plan at $6 and treat anything above $8 as a bug. The 2x tier above 272K tokens is per request and never approached.

nodes.norm_label: risk: cost per run under real traffic

nodes.label: Ideation unit economics estimate ($3-6 per image)
nodes.norm_label: ideation unit economics estimate ($3-6 per image)
nodes.rationale: Forty screenshot-driven steps resend their history for about 1.3M cumulative input tokens, mostly cached, plus ~30K output; assume the top of the range. The 2x tier past 272K input is charged per request, and a single request tops out near 63K.

nodes.label: Atomic free admission with microdollar spend reservations
nodes.norm_label: atomic free admission with microdollar spend reservations
nodes.rationale: One transaction refuses the fourth accepted run or a reservation that would exceed FREE_DAILY_BUDGET_USD; the reservation is the run's spend cap, and terminal completion replaces it with measured spend.

nodes.label: Astra agent loop
nodes.rationale: Send the instruction, screenshot history and step budget; execute the actions through EditorSession.act; screenshot and repeat. A step cap, a spend cap, model-produced narration and an explicit reasoning effort are not optional.

nodes.label: Browser provider shortlist (Browserbase, Anchor, Hyperbrowser, Steel)
nodes.norm_label: browser provider shortlist (browserbase, anchor, hyperbrowser, steel)
nodes.rationale: All expose a live-view iframe and a CDP endpoint from one session-create call; Steel Launch is disqualified at that tier because its fifteen-minute cap equals the run ceiling, and Anchor is noted for human handoff in a later version.

nodes.label: Browserbase
nodes.rationale: Default choice: the cheapest entry tier covering twenty concurrent runs, with a six-hour session length nowhere near binding.

nodes.label: Per-run cost estimate ($3.50 with caching, $14.50 without)
nodes.norm_label: per-run cost estimate ($3.50 with caching, $14.50 without)
nodes.rationale: The loop resends a growing screenshot history, so cost is quadratic in steps: forty steps send about 1.3M input tokens cumulatively, about $13 uncached against about $2 cached, plus about $1.50 of output.

nodes.label: Hosted Chrome session over CDP
nodes.rationale: One per run with Photopea loaded; needs CDP access, sessions of at least twenty minutes, concurrency for NFR-4 on the entry tier, and a live view.

nodes.label: Indirect prompt injection risk
nodes.rationale: The system card estimates an 8.5% attack success rate, and a confirmation policy barely moved unauthorised transactions (6.8%) or exfiltration (4.3%); asking the agent to confirm is not a control, making the bad action impossible is.

nodes.label: 272K-token long-request pricing tier
nodes.rationale: Not a risk: the 2x surcharge applies per request, forty frames come to about 63K tokens, and the step cap keeps it that way; exposure is cumulative, not per request.

nodes.label: Machine-local cache overflow above 15 requests per minute
nodes.norm_label: machine-local cache overflow above 15 requests per minute
nodes.rationale: Twenty concurrent runs exceed the threshold in total; whether it counts per cached prefix or across the organisation is unknown and decides which cost row launch day lands in.

nodes.label: Four run limits (step cap, spend cap, free runs, daily ceiling)
nodes.norm_label: four run limits (step cap, spend cap, free runs, daily ceiling)
nodes.rationale: Step and spend caps are enforced in the agent loop, free runs and the daily ceiling in the HTTP layer. A user-supplied key bypasses free runs and the ceiling but never the caps, since a runaway loop on someone else key is still our bug.

nodes.label: Secrets and upload handling
nodes.community_name: FR-36: user-supplied OpenAI API key, session-only, never written to disk or logs
nodes.rationale: Our key stays in the server environment; a user key lives in memory for the run and is redacted from logs; uploads go to object storage under an unguessable key with a 24-hour lifecycle, and results are served by signed URL.

nodes.label: Spike A2: step cap and frame window the cost allows
nodes.norm_label: spike a2: step cap and frame window the cost allows
nodes.rationale: Sizes the step cap so a run finishes inside fifteen minutes and sets the frame window and the measured cost per run the daily ceiling depends on.

nodes.label: Spike A4: OpenAI tier vs NFR-4
nodes.norm_label: spike a4: openai tier vs nfr-4
nodes.rationale: Day 0, one hour; the other spike that can still change the plan.

nodes.label: Aggressive prompt caching (4x unit-cost swing)
nodes.rationale: Not a tuning exercise: caching is the difference between a viable product and one that loses money on every image.

nodes.label: Metered credits business model
nodes.rationale: Never unmetered: three free images, then credits or bring-your-own-key, so one enthusiastic launch-day user cannot cost fifty dollars.

nodes.label: Hard step cap as a product parameter
nodes.norm_label: hard step cap as a product parameter
nodes.rationale: The cap is a product parameter, not a safety valve: a run that hits it returns whatever it has, layered.

nodes.label: Required FREE_DAILY_BUDGET_USD (no default daily ceiling)
nodes.rationale: Startup fails when the value is absent or invalid; the team-approved value and its concurrency arithmetic must be committed to the TRD before issue 29 closes.

nodes.label: User-supplied OpenAI key handling (bypasses admission, not per-run caps; never stored)
nodes.community_name: FR-36: user-supplied OpenAI API key, session-only, never written to disk or logs
nodes.norm_label: user-supplied openai key handling (bypasses admission, not per-run caps; never stored)
nodes.rationale: Passed directly to RunRequest.apiKey, retained only by the active run closure, redacted by construction from serializable state and released at terminal completion. The password-style form field is cleared when the start response arrives and never reaches sessionStorage, reducer state, analytics or error messages.

nodes.label: Bounded frame window
nodes.rationale: The first screenshot plus the last few, as the backstop if caching underperforms, at some cost in the model seeing its own work; the size is an output of spike A2.

nodes.label: Daily ceiling sized against concurrency, not one user
nodes.norm_label: daily ceiling sized against concurrency, not one user
nodes.rationale: Twenty concurrent runs at about $3.50 spend roughly $70 in one ten-minute wave, so a ceiling near fifty dollars trips on the first wave and NFR-4 holds only on paper; the number is a day-4 decision informed by spike A2.

nodes.label: Export-then-destroy session disposal
nodes.rationale: The session holds the only copy of the work, so FR-12 and FR-13 are unsatisfiable if teardown wins; export first on every path, best-effort on error, and never let a failed export block the teardown that stops the bill.

nodes.label: Fifteen-minute run ceiling
nodes.rationale: The single ceiling everywhere: the sixty-minute WebSocket lifetime is an outer bound and the twenty-minute provider session is margin. Sizing the step cap against sixty would make it four times too large.

nodes.label: No unit tests of model behaviour
nodes.norm_label: no unit tests of model behaviour
nodes.rationale: The model is not deterministic, and pretending otherwise wastes days the project does not have.

nodes.label: OpenAI tier rate limit as the concurrency ceiling
nodes.norm_label: openai tier rate limit as the concurrency ceiling
nodes.rationale: Tier 1 allows 500 requests and 500,000 tokens per minute with image tokens counted, which twenty runs exhaust before the server notices; raising the tier has a lead time, so it is checked on day 0.

nodes.label: Prompt caching strategy
nodes.rationale: The lever between about $3.50 and $14.50 per run: a byte-stable tool array frozen per run, a 1,024-token minimum prefix, a 30-minute TTL refreshed on reuse, and the implicit breakpoint at the last tool response.

nodes.label: Explicit reasoning.effort via configuration_update
nodes.rationale: The default is undocumented and none returns HTTP 400; the loop runs at low and raises to high for planning without disturbing the cached prefix.

nodes.label: Self-hosted Playwright remote Chrome (rejected)
nodes.rationale: A watchable, interruptible remote Chrome is weeks of work: arbitrating human takeover and keeping raw CDP (Runtime.evaluate, cookies) away from the user browser. If no provider works, the product changes instead.

nodes.label: Structural agent security controls
nodes.rationale: The browser reaches only the editor origin by network allow-list, the session holds no credentials, the instruction and image are untrusted input, and sessions are destroyed after every run.

nodes.label: Unattended-run system prompt
nodes.rationale: Astra is documented as tentative about when to stop and as over-obeying instruction files, so the prompt says the run is unattended and carries no decorative prohibitions; the user instruction is a separate untrusted message.

nodes.label: Computer use (primitive)
nodes.rationale: The highest-leverage primitive and the best silent GIF; desktop hosting, not computer use, made Round 1 unshippable.

nodes.label: Computer use x mid-turn steering (Round 9)
nodes.rationale: Crossing the two surviving primitives passes the Swap Test on both axes at once; the desktop scope gate falls away once the target is web-based professional software.

nodes.label: Hosted-browser computer use (Round 2)
nodes.rationale: Removes the desktop VM fleet, but pointed at services it lands in crowded startup categories; the lesson is to point it at software instead.

nodes.label: ag-psd fallback
nodes.rationale: Writes layered PSDs from Node with no browser; a strictly worse product with nothing to watch or steer and no model leverage. The floor, not a plan: choosing it means the launch copy stops claiming computer use.

nodes.label: Embedded Photopea driven by the user (fallback product)
nodes.norm_label: embedded photopea driven by the user (fallback product)
nodes.rationale: A cross-origin iframe gives the parent page no pixels, and the agent input is pixels, so embedding only works for a weaker product where the agent writes scripts rather than looking.

nodes.label: Ideation kill gates (scope, crowding)
nodes.rationale: Scope (five build days, no hosted desktop VM fleet) and crowding (existing startup categories, prior hackathon winners) removed ideas that passed the Swap Test.

nodes.label: Web-based professional software unlock
nodes.rationale: Round 1's fatal gate was "desktop", not computer use; GUI-locked, API-poor web apps such as Figma, Google Sheets and Photopea run in a hosted browser with no VM fleet or licence server.

nodes.label: .agents/skills/ skills directory
nodes.rationale: Holds installed and local skills in one place; .claude/skills/ symlinks to it instead of keeping a copy.

nodes.label: AGENTS.md (agent instruction entry point)
nodes.rationale: Entry point for every agent harness. It states what the repository builds (Layerhand, an agent that retouches photographs inside a real image editor and returns a layered file, for the OpenAI x Product Hunt GPT-6 Astra Challenge) and @-imports eleven documents in three groups, each with a note on what it covers: instructions (Andrej Karpathy skills, graphify, RTK, project conventions, skills), references (git workflow, Markdown style guide) and project documents (PRODUCT, PRD, TRD, Product Hunt ideas). Harnesses without import support open the files directly. CLAUDE.md and GEMINI.md are symlinks to it, so edits go to AGENTS.md only.

nodes.label: AGENTS.md as the single agent entry point
nodes.norm_label: agents.md as the single agent entry point
nodes.rationale: AGENTS.md is symlinked as CLAUDE.md and GEMINI.md, so every agent reads the same instructions. Edit AGENTS.md itself, never either symlink.

nodes.label: NFR-6: uploaded images deleted within twenty-four hours
nodes.community_name: FR-36: user-supplied OpenAI API key, session-only, never written to disk or logs
nodes.norm_label: nfr-6: uploaded images deleted within twenty-four hours

nodes.label: Code-execution tool over a persistent Playwright session
nodes.norm_label: code-execution tool over a persistent playwright session
nodes.rationale: The planned mechanism, the reverse of what the ideation assumed: OpenAI recommends it for Astra and it is likely more reliable, while the editor still has no usable API.

nodes.label: computer tool (GA)
nodes.rationale: The GA definition is exactly {type: computer}; kept as the fallback because the guide says it remains supported as an alternative and its examples are pinned to the previous generation.

nodes.label: Editor adapter
nodes.rationale: The only component that knows which editor is driven; everything else sees Contract 1. Its one design rule is the scripted vs driven split.

nodes.label: Orchestrator
nodes.rationale: The only component that talks to the model, so the model choice cannot leak past it.

nodes.label: OpenAI Responses API (gpt-6-astra)
nodes.rationale: Chat Completions does not support function calling with Astra at all.

nodes.label: Spike A0: code execution or the computer tool
nodes.norm_label: spike a0: code execution or the computer tool
nodes.rationale: Day 0, half a day; runs both mechanisms against the same three-edit sequence and is one of the two spikes that can still change the plan.

nodes.label: FR-16: per-user history of past runs (P2, deferred by the non-goals)
nodes.norm_label: fr-16: per-user history of past runs (p2, deferred by the non-goals)
nodes.rationale: The product brief's non-goals rule out both history and accounts, so it waits until those are revisited after launch.

nodes.label: Requirement-level exclusions (no accounts, no in-app editing, no undo, PSD-only output, no internationalisation)
nodes.norm_label: requirement-level exclusions (no accounts, no in-app editing, no undo, psd-only output, no internationalisation)
nodes.rationale: The product brief's non-goals are binding on the PRD; the free allowance is enforced without identity, and the app shows the run and hands back a file rather than offering editing.

nodes.label: Product non-goals (no image generation, no batch/API/integrations, no accounts beyond metering, no mobile, no own editor, no presets)
nodes.norm_label: product non-goals (no image generation, no batch/api/integrations, no accounts beyond metering, no mobile, no own editor, no presets)
nodes.rationale: Stated so that nobody builds them in the six build days available; a per-client house style is the obvious second product, not the first.

nodes.label: Fenced code blocks with a declared language
nodes.norm_label: fenced code blocks with a declared language
nodes.rationale: Indented blocks cannot name a language, have ambiguous boundaries and are harder to find in Code Search. Declare the language so neither the highlighter nor the next editor must guess, escape newlines in copyable shell snippets, and indent blocks nested in lists.

nodes.label: FR-1: accept one JPEG/PNG image up to 20 MB and 6000 px
nodes.norm_label: fr-1: accept one jpeg/png image up to 20 mb and 6000 px

nodes.label: EXIF orientation-aware expected dimensions
nodes.rationale: From the September 15 regression: a 32x16 JPEG with orientation 6 displays as 16x32, so bounded APP1/TIFF IFD0 parsing supplies displayed dimensions (orientations 5-8 swap axes); malformed inspected EXIF is rejected before boot, while original bytes and the long-edge limit are unchanged.

nodes.label: Upload validation before session creation
nodes.rationale: Format by magic bytes, size by actual body length, and dimensions read from the header, each with its own message; a session opened for an upload that will be rejected is a bill paid for nothing.

nodes.label: Spike B2: Browserbase signup and cold-start measurement
nodes.norm_label: spike b2: browserbase signup and cold-start measurement
nodes.rationale: No longer a comparison: sign up, create one real session, confirm live view and CDP, and measure the unpublished cold start.

nodes.label: Bun full-stack HTML import (src/server/index.ts serves src/web/index.html)
nodes.norm_label: bun full-stack html import (src/server/index.ts serves src/web/index.html)
nodes.rationale: Bun bundles the HTML, TypeScript, CSS, fonts and images with one bun build --target=bun command, so no React, router, CSS framework or second development server is added.

nodes.label: Environment configuration names (DATABASE_URL, SESSION_SECRET, FREE_DAILY_BUDGET_USD, S3_*, BROWSERBASE_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, TRUST_PROXY_HOPS)
nodes.norm_label: environment configuration names (database_url, session_secret, free_daily_budget_usd, s3_*, browserbase_api_key, openai_api_key, trust_proxy_hops)
nodes.rationale: .env.example documents names and formats without working credentials, and configuration parsing reports missing variable names, never values.

nodes.label: /health readiness endpoint (process and database readiness)
nodes.rationale: Reports readiness but never returns configuration values.

nodes.label: HTTP surface aligned with Contract 3 plus /health
nodes.norm_label: http surface aligned with contract 3 plus /health

nodes.label: Two-stage non-root container pinned to Bun 1.4.2
nodes.norm_label: two-stage non-root container pinned to bun 1.4.2
nodes.rationale: Exposes one port, runs as a non-root user, stores no secret in an image layer, and starts the compiled server.

nodes.label: Idempotent waitlist endpoint and CSV export (bun run waitlist:export)
nodes.norm_label: idempotent waitlist endpoint and csv export (bun run waitlist:export)
nodes.rationale: Normalizes and trims the address, rejects malformed or oversized input, and treats an existing address as a successful submission; the export writes CSV to standard output.

nodes.label: Local development (bun install --frozen-lockfile, bun run dev, localhost:3000, /health)
nodes.norm_label: local development (bun install --frozen-lockfile, bun run dev, localhost:3000, /health)
nodes.rationale: Copy .env.example to .env only for local development; production values live in the deployment platform's secret store.

nodes.label: Verification commands (bun test, typecheck, lint, build, container smoke test)
nodes.norm_label: verification commands (bun test, typecheck, lint, build, container smoke test)
nodes.rationale: Tests requiring live providers are opt-in and skip without their explicit environment variables.

nodes.label: Layerhand README
nodes.rationale: Layerhand works inside a real image editor, streams visible progress, accepts corrections during a run, and returns a layered PSD rather than only a flattened image.

nodes.label: Bun 1.4.2 runtime pin (lockfile version 2, frozen installs)
nodes.norm_label: bun 1.4.2 runtime pin (lockfile version 2, frozen installs)
nodes.rationale: The committed bun.lock uses lockfile version 2, which Bun 1.3 cannot read; installs and container builds use --frozen-lockfile and must fail rather than regenerate an unreadable lockfile.
